messages.subject: integrate with new unmarked version?
parts:
Dear unmarked users/founders,

...hope you can help me:)
I was fighting a bit with the 'integrate' function to get a eshw
value from my detection function (fit with hazard rate model). Indeed
with the latest version of unmarked I got the following:


integrate(gxhaz,0,20,shape=4.21, scale=0.98)$value
Error in f(x, ...) : unused argument(s) (shape = 4.21, scale = 0.98)

I decided then simply to try to use a previous version of unmarked,
and then, don't know really why it worked:

integrate(gxhaz, 0, 20, shape=4.21, scale=0.98)$value
[1] 8.831198

Could someone help me figure out what I did wrong or what have changed
within the latest version concerning that topic?

Basically I then want to find mean detection prob. value for my
function...was wondering if using eshw/(distance max) was the only to
get this value? From the Detection values (estimate, SE, z, P) of such
a function below, isn't it possible to infer it?

haz_Null <- distsamp(~1 ~ 1, umf, keyfun = "hazard")
haz_Null

Detection:
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
1.44 2.37 0.606 0.544

Can hardly intrepret these value...maybe I should get back to the
basic (Buckland et al.) for such a trivial question?


Thanks for any help or comments,

Kevin

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] integrate with new unmarked version?
parts:
Hi Kevin,

What version of unmarked were you using when you got that error? I just tried it on 0.9-3 and it works fine.

You are correct that to obtain an estimate of detection probability, you divide the integral by the maximum distance. Note that you need to use gxhaz for line transects and grhaz for point counts. We should add some more user friendly functions for this stuff. Note that you can use getP() to get estimates of detection probability for each distance interval. Sum these up for each transect to get transect-level estimates of detection probability.

Regarding, the estimates returned by distsamp. These could be labeled better, but they are the estimates of the parameters of the detection function (on the log-scale).

Richard

Richard

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] integrate with new unmarked version?
parts:
Hello list,

I'm attempting to a model a suite of base detection functions (Poisson and Negative Binomial) in gdistsamp prior to modeling my candidates that incorporate covariates which may influence abundance, availability and detection.

A little background: birds were sampled at 189 point counts 3 times during a season (1 primary period, 3 secondary periods). I'm using 6 landcover classes (% A,B,C...F), % road, and well density and patch size as siteCov. I'm using Julian date of survey and average wind speed as yearlySiteCovs. All covariates are included in the unmarkedFrameGDS that is then used to select the best fitting detection function (hazard rate P, half normal NB, etc.).

y data (distance) = 189 x 21 matrix                    (site ID in multinomial that corresponds to 7 distance bins x 3 survey periods)
siteCovs = 189 observations of 10 variables         (site ID, 9 covariates)
yearlysiteCovs = 189 observations of 7 variables  (site ID, 3 date columns, 3 wind columns)

The abbreviated process (excluding correlation tests, standardizing covariates, etc) looks like this:

## Import distance data (i.e., "y") into R

DIST1 = read.delim(file = "GRSP_SP1_DIST.txt", header=TRUE,sep="\t", colClasses=c("factor","numeric","factor","numeric","numeric"))

## Import covariate (i.e., "siteCovs") data into R

COVS = read.delim("GRSP_COVS.txt",header = TRUE,sep = "\t",colClasses= c(rep("numeric",10),"factor","factor"))

## Import observation covariate (i.e., "yearlySiteCovs") data into R

YRCOVS = read.delim("GRSP_YRCOVS.txt", header = TRUE, sep="\t", colClasses = c("factor","numeric","numeric","numeric","numeric","numeric","numeric"))

## Format distance data into multinomial format

db <- seq(0,140,by=20)
y.dat1 = formatDistData(distData = DIST1, distCol = "dist", transectNameCol="id", dist.breaks=db, occasionCol="round")

## Combine multinomial data in unmarkedframeGDS

umfsp1 <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y = as.matrix(y.dat1), siteCovs = COVS, numPrimary = 1, yearlySiteCovs = YRCOVS, dist.breaks = db, survey = "point", unitsIn = "m")

## Add detection models to list.
basedetect <- list()

## Fit base detection models.

basedetect$hn.P = gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1, umfsp1, keyfun="halfnorm", mixture="P", unitsOut="kmsq",output="density",K=200)
basedetect$haz.P = gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1, umfsp1, keyfun="hazard", mixture="P", unitsOut="kmsq",output="density",K=200)
basedetect$exp.P = gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1, umfsp1, keyfun="exp", mixture="P", unitsOut="kmsq",output="density",K=200)
.......

Similar to the integrate error Kevin received (in this thread) I receive this error message:

Error in integrate(grhn, db[j], db[j + 1], sigma = sigma[i, t], rel.tol = rel.tol,  : 
  a limit is missing

As Chandler and Royal suggested elsewhere in this group, I've adjusted rel.tot. and start values with a range of +/- and 0 values to correct the integrate issue.

basedetect$hn.P = gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1, umfsp1, keyfun="halfnorm", mixture="P", unitsOut="kmsq",starts=c(1,1,1),rel.tol=0.001,output="density",K=200)

No combination of values corrects the error. I've tried stripping the yearlysiteCovs out of the unmarkedFrame to no avail. I've checked  the str() of the files and it appears all my factor and numeric designations are correct.  Was this a software issue like Kevin alluded to in the first post?  Truthfully, I have more faith in the software than my own abilities :).  I'm stumped.

Can anyone offer some advice?

Thanks in advance, Erik

Using:
RStudio v. 0.97.310
unmarked v. 0.9-9 with typical dependencies (plyr, RcppArmadillo, reshape)

## Import distance data (i.e., "y") into R

parts:
Hi Richard,

Indeed, the solution was as simple as changing the numPrimary from a 1 to a 3 in the UMF - no more integrate error. This change also fixed the error: "Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) : initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite" I received when modeling the uniform P & NB detection functions.

So the take home for me is: in gdistsamp, when analyzing one season with multiple (secondary) samples per location, the number of secondary surveys (3 sample my case) needs to be specified when y is formatted in 'formatDistData' using 'occasionCol.'  When the unmarkedFrame is created, the number of secondary surveys within the season is now designated as 'numPrimary.' A little counter intuitive but now I understand.

As always thank you for your help and until next time, Erik
